research.title: The Developer is the New Perimeter: How Supply Chain Attacks Are Becoming Cloud Breaches

research.title: Oh Look, The Foot Gun Went Off Again (Citrix NetScaler PreAuth Command Injection CVE-2026-88771)

research.title: Master Key Included: Detecting SolarWinds ARM CVE-2026-28326
research.summary: A hardcoded authentication secret ships with every SolarWinds Access Rights Manager install, and reaching TCP 55555 is enough to hit a .NET deserialization sink. Bishop Fox confirmed SYSTEM-level code execution, breaks down the root cause, and shares a safe.

research.title: AI-powered fuzzing with the GitHub Security Lab Taskflow Agent

research.title: Trust and the enticing consultancy offer

research.title: Fewer Findings, Faster Answers: How ActiveState and Trivy Turn a Scan Into a Verdict
research.summary: Trivy, the open source security scanner maintained by Aqua Security, is one of the most widely trusted tools for identifying vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and secrets across containers, code, IaC, and Kubernetes. Millions of scans run against it every.

research.title: Unified Code, Unified Risks: Uncovering Vulnerabilities in .NET MAUI Applications
research.summary: .NET MAUI lets developers write once and ship to both platforms. From an attacker's perspective, that means reverse-engineer once and break everywhere. This post walks through extracting readable assemblies from MAUI apps and the high-impact vulnerability.

research.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Sol: An evaluation
research.summary: Compared with GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol writes 27% less code and produces 22% fewer findings in total, at a pass rate 2.76 points lower and with more findings per line of code. GPT-6 Astra was the release where correctness and volume improved together. Astra.
